source.title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation

accepted.question_text: For a real number x, let ||x|| denote the distance from x to the nearest integer. For each integer n >= 2 and every n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must lim inf as q tends to infinity of q ||q theta_1|| ... ||q theta_n|| equal 0?

evidence.quote: here and in the sequel || · || stands for the distance to the nearest integer
The similar multidimensional problem is for given n ⩾ 2 to prove that for any reals θ1 , ..., θn one has lim inf q ||qθ1 || · · · ||qθn || = 0.
This problem is not solved for any n ⩾ 2.

accepted.question_text: Let Lambda be a full-rank lattice in R^(n+1). Define its homogeneous minimum N(Lambda) as the infimum of |z_0 z_1 ... z_n| over all nonzero z = (z_0, z_1, ..., z_n) in Lambda. Call a lattice algebraic when it is obtained from the embeddings of a basis 1, theta_1, ..., theta_n of a totally real algebraic field of degree n+1, followed by multiplication by a diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries. For n >= 2, must every lattice Lambda with N(Lambda) > 0 be algebraic?

evidence.quote: Suppose that 1, θ1 , ..., θn form a basis of a totally real algebraic field K = Q(θ) of degree n + 1.
Let G be a diagonal matrix of dimension (n+1)×(n+1) with non-zero diagonal elements. We consider a lattice of the form Λ = G Ω Zn+1 . Lattices of such a type are known as algebraic lattices.
For an arbitrary lattice Λ ⊂ Rn+1 we consider its homogeneous minima N (Λ) = inf |z0 z1 · · · zn |.
A famous Oppenheim conjecture supposes that in the case n ⩾ 2 any lattice Λ satisfying N (L) > 0 is an algebraic lattice. This conjecture is still open.

accepted.question_text: Let p be a prime. For an integer n = p^nu n_1 with gcd(n_1,p)=1, define the p-adic norm by |n|_p = p^(-nu). For every real number theta, must lim inf as q tends to infinity of q |q|_p ||q theta|| equal 0? Equivalently, for every irrational theta, must inf over positive integers n and q of q ||p^n q theta|| equal 0?

evidence.quote: Let for a prime p consider the p-adic norm | · |p, that is if n = pν n1 , (n1 , p) = 1, ν ∈ Z+ then |n|p = p−ν .
De Mathan and Teulié conjectured [93] that for any θ ∈ R one has lim inf q|q|p ||qθ|| = 0.
The conjecture can be reformulated as follows: to prove or to disprove that for irrational θ one has inf q||pn qθ|| = 0.

accepted.question_text: Let M >= 2 and let (t_j) be a sequence of positive real numbers satisfying t_{j+1}/t_j >= 1 + 1/M for all positive integers j. Peres and Schlag proved that there is an absolute constant gamma > 0 such that every such sequence admits a real alpha with ||alpha t_j|| >= gamma/(M log M) for all j. What is the correct optimal order, as a function of M, of the largest universal lower bound that can be forced in this homogeneous problem? In particular, can the gamma/(M log M) bound be improved?

evidence.quote: Suppose that for some M ⩾ 2 one has tj+1 / tj ⩾ 1 + 1/M, ∀j ∈ Z+ .
Then with a certain absolute constant γ > 0 for any sequence {tj } under the condition (10) there exists real α such that ||αtj || ⩾ γ / (M log M), ∀j ∈ Z+.
The open question is to find the right order of approximation in the homogeneous version of this problem. In general Peres-Schlag’s method does not give optimal bounds.
The conjecture is that Theorem 9 may be improved on, and the optimal result should be stronger than the inequality (11).

accepted.question_text: Do there exist real numbers theta_1 and theta_2 that are linearly independent over Z together with 1, real shifts eta_1 and eta_2, and a constant psi_0 > 0 such that inf over positive integers x of x psi_0 ||theta_1 x - eta_1|| ||theta_2 x - eta_2|| is positive? A negative answer would give a stronger inhomogeneous form of Littlewood's conjecture.

evidence.quote: Then there exist real numbers θ1 , θ2 linearly independent over Z together with 1 and real numbers η1 , η2 such that inf xψ(x) · ||α1 x − η1 || · ||α2x − η2 || > 0.

The following problem is an open one: is it possible that for a constant function ψ(t) = ψ0 > 0 ∀t the conclusion of Theorem 8 remains true. If not, it means that a stronger inhomogeneous version of Littlewood conjecture is valid.

accepted.question_text: Fix alpha,beta in (0,1) with alpha + beta = 1. For theta = (theta_1,theta_2), consider the set of shifts eta = (eta_1,eta_2) in R^2 for which inf over q of max(q^alpha ||q theta_1 - eta_1||, q^beta ||q theta_2 - eta_2||) is positive. Harrap proved that this shift set has full Hausdorff dimension when theta belongs to BAD(alpha,beta). Does the same full-Hausdorff-dimension statement, and even the Schmidt-game winning property, hold without assuming theta belongs to BAD(alpha,beta)?

evidence.quote: For α, β ∈ [0, 1] under the condition α + β = 1 and δ > 0 we consider the sets BAD(α, β; δ)

Harrap [57] proved that given α, β ∈ (0, 1), α + β = 1 for a fixed vector (θ1 , θ2 ) ∈ BAD(α, β) the set {(η1 , η2 ) ∈ R2 : inf max(q α ||qθ1 − η1 ||, q β ||qθ2 − η2 || > 0} has full Hausdorff dimension.
The following question formulated by Harrap [57]: to prove that the set (9) is a set of full Hausdorff dimension (and even a winning set) without the condition (8).

accepted.question_text: Fix positive integers m and n, norms on R^m and R^n, and a real n by m matrix Theta such that Theta x is not in Z^n for every nonzero x in Z^m. Let z_nu = (x_nu,y_nu) be the sequence of best-approximation vectors, set M_nu = |x_nu|, and define G(Theta) = lim inf as nu tends to infinity of M_nu^(1/nu). What are the optimal lower bounds for inf G(Theta), where the infimum ranges over all such matrices Theta for the fixed dimensions and norms?

evidence.quote: Suppose that Θx 6∈ Zn , ∀x ∈ Zm \ {0}.
Let zν = (xν , yν ) ∈ Zm+n , x ∈ Zm , y ∈ Zn , ν = 1, 2, 3, ... be the infinite sequence of best approximation vectors
We are interested in the value G(Θ) = lim inf Mν1/ν.
The general problem is to find optimal bounds for the value inf G(Θ) for fixed dimensions m, n and for fixed norms | · |m∗ , | · |n∗.

accepted.question_text: Let theta_1 and theta_2 be real numbers linearly independent over Z together with 1. For positive integers x_1,x_2, define psi_+(t) as the minimum of ||theta_1 x_1 + theta_2 x_2|| over 0 < max(x_1,x_2) <= t, and define omega_+(theta_1,theta_2) as the supremum of gamma such that lim inf as t tends to infinity of t^gamma psi_+(t) is finite. What is the optimal value of inf omega_+(theta_1,theta_2) over linearly independent pairs? Is it the golden ratio phi, the exponent sigma discussed in the same setting, or some value between them?

evidence.quote: We are interested in small values of the linear form ||θ1 x1 + ... + θn xn || in positive integers x1 , ..., xn .
ψ+ (t) = ψ+;Θ (t) = min ||θ1 x1 + ... + θm xm ||.
ω+ = ω+ (Θ) = sup{γ : lim inf tγ ψ+;Θ (t) < ∞}
What is the optimal exponent inf θ1 ,θ2 − independent ω+ (Θ) in the problem for a linear form in two positive variables? Is it φ or σ or something else between φ and σ?

accepted.question_text: For an integer m >= 3, let 1, theta_1, ..., theta_m be linearly independent over Z. Define psi_+(t) from the minimum of ||theta_1 x_1 + ... + theta_m x_m|| over positive integers x_i with 0 < max_i x_i <= t, and define omega_+ as the supremum of gamma such that lim inf t^gamma psi_+(t) is finite. Does there exist such a collection 1, theta_1, ..., theta_m with omega_+ < 2, already for m = 3 or even for arbitrary m >= 3?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of omega plus below two

evidence.quote: ψ+ (t) = ψ+;Θ (t) = min ||θ1 x1 + ... + θm xm ||.
ω+ = ω+ (Θ) = sup{γ : lim inf tγ ψ+;Θ (t) < ∞}
But in view of Theorem 18 I may conjecture that for m = 3 (or even for an arbitrary m) there exist a collection of linearly independent numbers 1, θ1 , ..., θm such that ω+ (Θ) < 2.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant k such that for every positive integer q there is an integer a coprime to q whose finite continued fraction expansion a/q = [b_0; b_1, ..., b_s] has all partial quotients b_j, for j >= 1, bounded by k? Zaremba's original stronger guess is that k = 5 suffices.

evidence.quote: For an irreducible rational fraction aq ∈ Q we consider its continued fraction expansion a/q = [b0 ; b1 , . . . , bs ]

The famous Zaremba’s conjecture [154] supposes that there exists an absolute constant k with the following property: for any positive integer q there exists a coprime to q such that in the continued fraction expansion (53) all partial quotients are bounded
In fact Zaremba conjectured that k = 5.

accepted.question_text: Fix positive integers s and q with gcd(s,q)=1, and fix a digit set D = {d_0,...,d_k} satisfying 0=d_0<d_1<...<d_k<s, 1 <= k <= s-2, and gcd(d_1,...,d_k)=1. Let K_s^D(N) be the set of positive integers x<N whose base-s digits all lie in D. Does there exist a sufficiently large sigma>0 such that, whenever N >= q^sigma, every residue class lambda modulo q is represented by some x in K_s^D(N)?

evidence.quote: KsD (N) = {x ∈ Z+ : x < N, x = Σ δj sj , δj ∈ D}.
Suppose that (s, q) = (d0 , ..., dk ) = 1, k ⩾ 2. Is it true that for some large σ > 0 for N ⩾ qσ for any λ (mod q) there exists x ∈ KsD (N) such that x ≡ λ (mod q) ?

accepted.question_text: Let p be prime, U a multiplicative subgroup of Z_p^*, v a nonzero residue class, and R = vU. A known result assumes #R >= 10^8 p^(7/8) log^(5/2) p and then finds an element a in R whose continued-fraction partial quotients for a/p have sum at most 500 log p log log p, yielding D(a,p) << log p log log p. Can the exponent 7/8 in the subgroup-size hypothesis be replaced by a smaller exponent while retaining such a conclusion?

evidence.quote: Let p be prime, U be a multiplicative subgroup in Z∗p . For v 6= 0 we consider the set R = v · U and let #R ≥ 108 p7/8 log5/2 p.
Then there exists an element a ∈ R, a/p = [b1 , b2 , · · · , bl ], bi = bi (a), l = l(a) with Σ bi ≤ 500 log p log log p, and hence D(a, p) ≪ log p log log p.
An open problem here is as follows. Is it possible to replace exponent 7/8 in the condition (63) by a smaller one?

accepted.question_text: For dimension s >= 2 and positive integer q, define the discrepancy D(a_1,...,a_s;q) of the Korobov-Hlawka point sequence ((a_1 k/q), ({a_2 k/q}), ..., ({a_s k/q})) for 0 <= k <= q-1 by taking the supremum over axis-aligned boxes [0,gamma_1) x ... x [0,gamma_s) of the absolute deviation from q gamma_1...gamma_s. Is it true that min over integer vectors (a_1,...,a_s) of D(a_1,...,a_s;q) is O_s((log q)^(s-1))? Equivalently, can the extra log log q factor in Bykovskii's bound be removed?

evidence.quote: We are interested in upper bounds for the discrepancy D(a1 , ..., as ; q) = sup |#{k : ξk ∈ [0, γ1 ) × · · · × [0, γs )} − qγ1 · · · γs |.
Theorem 30. For s ⩾ 2 one has and for any positive integer q one has min D(a1 , ..., as ; q) ≪s (log q)s−1 log log q.
A famous well-known conjecture is that min D(a1 , ..., as ; q) ≪s (log q)s−1 , that is that the factor log log q in (64) may be thrown away.

accepted.question_text: Let F_n be the Stern-Brocot sequence at level n, written in increasing order as 0 = xi_{0,n} < xi_{1,n} < ... < xi_{2^n,n} = 1. Define R_n by the identity sum_{j=1}^{2^n} (xi_{j,n} - j/2^n)^2 = 2^n integral from 0 to 1 of (?(x)-x)^2 dx + R_n, where ? is Minkowski's question mark function. Is R_n -> 0 as n -> infinity?

evidence.quote: It will be important for us to recall the definition of Stern-Brocot sequences Fn , n = 0, 1, 2, . . . .
Suppose that the sequence Fn is written in the increasing order 0 = ξ0,n < ξ1,n < · · · < ξN (n),n = 1, N(n) = 2n
That is why we have Σ (ξj,n − j/2n)2 = 2n ∫ (?(x) − x)2 dx + Rn , |Rn | ⩽ 4.
The question is as follows. Is it true that for the remainder in (67) one has Rn → 0 as n → ∞?

accepted.question_text: For lambda in (0,1), let g_lambda be the Denjoy-Tichy-Uitz singular function on [0,1], defined by g_lambda(0)=0, g_lambda(1)=1, and by the Farey recursion g_lambda((a+c)/(b+d)) = (1-lambda)g_lambda(a/b) + lambda g_lambda(c/d) for neighboring Farey fractions a/b < c/d, with extension to irrational x by continuity. For an irrational x=[a_0; a_1,a_2,...], set S_x(t)=a_1+...+a_t. Define kappa_1(lambda) as the supremum of kappa such that lim sup S_x(t)/t < kappa implies g_lambda'(x)=+infinity, and define kappa_2(lambda) as the infimum of kappa such that lim inf S_x(t)/t > kappa implies g_lambda'(x)=0. What are the functions kappa_1(lambda) and kappa_2(lambda) for 0<lambda<1?

trace.notes: Normalized the original input as a zbMATH resolver URL with document identifier 900135982.

Direct browser access to the zbMATH resolver did not expose readable technical text. A local source index row for zbMATH identifier 900135982 identified the exact work title and arXiv link https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4539.

Resolved the exact work to arXiv:1202.4539 and used the locally available PDF artifact .sisyphus/paper-question-parser/tmp/1202.4539.pdf for page-numbered extraction; the canonical resolved locator is https://arxiv.org/pdf/1202.4539.pdf.

Mapped a 42-page survey titled 'On some open problems in Diophantine approximation'. Open-problem regions occur in Sections 1, 2, 4.5, 5, and 6, with concentrated question material on pages 1, 3-8, 11-17, 22-23, 27-31, and 34.
Extracted Littlewood-type, Oppenheim-lattice, p-adic, inhomogeneous, Harrap, and Peres-Schlag questions from Section 1.
Extracted best-approximation and positive-integer Diophantine-exponent questions from Sections 2 and 4.5.
Extracted Zaremba, missing-digits, subgroup-exponent, and discrepancy questions from Section 5.
Extracted Minkowski question mark function and Denjoy-Tichy-Uitz family questions from Section 6.

Expanded accepted questions with source-supported definitions for ||x||, p-adic norm, algebraic lattices, best-approximation vectors, omega-plus, missing-digit sets, discrepancy, Stern-Brocot sequences, and g_lambda.

Moved candidates to needs_review when formulas were ambiguous in the source text or when the candidate depended on unresolved numbered equations or definitions not recoverable from the extracted evidence.

Kept distinct questions separate when they concerned different mathematical objects or different asymptotic regimes, including the main Zaremba conjecture versus discrepancy consequences and the separate fixed-point and Stern-Brocot remainder questions for the question mark function.

Accepted items include page-numbered evidence and avoid source-pointing references in question_text; items with ambiguous formulas, unresolved cross-references, or insufficient evidence for a precise standalone rewrite were kept in needs_review.
